title: Art bible · Early references
summary:
Collected references for World in Dreams. The owner selected **Isekai 01 — Axel** for settlement-scale composition and **Isekai 04 + 05 — Re:Zero and Overlord** for more distant world views. These are source images, separate from the generated concepts in Art bible → Overview.

All twelve references and their original source notes are preserved.

items.title: Isekai 01 · KonoSuba — Axel
items.alt: Aerial anime city: a compact walled footprint, dense warm roofs, a river and roads radiating through districts.
items.body:
**Classic isekai references · primary inspiration**

**Visible in this image:** Aerial anime city: a compact walled footprint, dense warm roofs, a river and roads radiating through districts.

**Top-down translation — proposal:** Use as the main everyday adventurer-town mood reference. In top-down, preserve the relationship between river, bridges, gates and streets; vary the outline and districts with terrain.

**Source and camera limits:** Anime image reproduced in a secondary architecture blog. The image has an oblique aerial camera and strong sun streaks; neither is the target camera or lighting treatment.

Existing reference artwork; rights remain with its respective owners. This is not a generated World in Dreams asset.

items.title: Isekai 02 · Overlord — E-Rantel city plan
items.alt: A near-plan view shows concentric defensive rings and radial connections, with part of the plan obscured by a foreground character.
items.body:
**Classic isekai references · primary inspiration**

**Visible in this image:** A near-plan view shows concentric defensive rings and radial connections, with part of the plan obscured by a foreground character.

**Top-down translation — proposal:** Study controlled entrances, defensive depth and districts. Translate those into a readable top-down fortified city template.

**Source and camera limits:** A fan-shared image identified as E-Rantel by its uploader. Episode and original publication provenance have not been independently verified; this is not presented as a complete surveyed map.

Existing reference artwork; rights remain with its respective owners. This is not a generated World in Dreams asset.

items.title: Isekai 03 · Re:Zero — Priestella
items.alt: A high aerial view reveals a circular urban footprint, waterways and strong connections between sectors.
items.body:
**Classic isekai references · primary inspiration**

**Visible in this image:** A high aerial view reveals a circular urban footprint, waterways and strong connections between sectors.

**Top-down translation — proposal:** A water-city template: canals separate districts while bridges and gates become clear route bottlenecks.

**Source and camera limits:** Teaser-PV frame reproduced by Comic Natalie. Near-overhead perspective is useful, but foreground feathers and cinematic light obscure parts of the plan; omit those in future top-down concepts.

Existing reference artwork; rights remain with its respective owners. This is not a generated World in Dreams asset.

items.title: Isekai 04 · Re:Zero — regional world view
items.alt: An illustrated regional map connects small settlement symbols, woodland masses, mountains and dotted travel routes.
items.body:
**Classic isekai references · primary inspiration**

**Visible in this image:** An illustrated regional map connects small settlement symbols, woodland masses, mountains and dotted travel routes.

**Top-down translation — proposal:** Use for world-scale hierarchy: a city, village, estate and landmark should read differently before zooming into architecture.

**Source and camera limits:** Reproduced in AnimeClick coverage of the game-map reveal. This is a game-associated illustrated map, not an exhaustive world atlas; do not infer precise geography or distances from it.

Existing reference artwork; rights remain with its respective owners. This is not a generated World in Dreams asset.

items.title: Isekai 05 · Overlord — regional geography
items.alt: A parchment-like regional map uses different settlement symbols, mountain chains, forests and boundaries.
items.body:
**Classic isekai references · primary inspiration**

**Visible in this image:** A parchment-like regional map uses different settlement symbols, mountain chains, forests and boundaries.

**Top-down translation — proposal:** Use for the relation between realms, terrain barriers and settlement hierarchy. The current world viewer can keep terrain colours while borrowing the symbol hierarchy.

**Source and camera limits:** Anime map reproduced in a secondary episode blog. This studies cartographic organisation, not a proposed parchment filter for the game.

Existing reference artwork; rights remain with its respective owners. This is not a generated World in Dreams asset.

items.title: 01 · Rural beginnings
items.alt: A small clearing with a few buildings and branching paths.
items.body:
**Early references · Foundation**

**What to study:** A small clearing with a few buildings and branching paths.

**World in Dreams use:** Human and halfling villages: leave space for fields, storage and later growth.

**Boundary:** The quiet, rounded forms are useful; the sparse clearing alone does not explain a complete food-producing village.

Publisher-provided screenshot, retained here as a local research reference. Artwork belongs to its respective owners; it is not an original project asset.

items.title: 02 · A town with a readable centre
items.alt: Warm roof groups, timber framing and a taller civic landmark organise the streets.
items.body:
**Early references · Foundation**

**What to study:** Warm roof groups, timber framing and a taller civic landmark organise the streets.

**World in Dreams use:** Human towns and mixed trading cities: group houses into neighbourhoods and give the market a clear centre.

**Boundary:** Study massing and street hierarchy; do not reproduce the specific buildings or the interface.

Publisher-provided screenshot, retained here as a local research reference. Artwork belongs to its respective owners; it is not an original project asset.

items.title: 03 · A working coastal settlement
items.alt: Fields, houses, a landing and wooded slopes form one connected settlement.
items.body:
**Early references · Pioneers of Pagonia**

**What to study:** Fields, houses, a landing and wooded slopes form one connected settlement.

**World in Dreams use:** A village that supplies a nearby city: make the route from production to storage to transport visible.

**Boundary:** Secondary reference for visible production and settlement organisation. Classic isekai images above now lead the visual direction.

Publisher-provided screenshot, retained here as a local research reference. Artwork belongs to its respective owners; it is not an original project asset.

items.title: 04 · The world at a glance
items.alt: Forests, rivers, fields and roof clusters form distinct colour masses from above.
items.body:
**Early references · Dorfromantik**

**What to study:** Forests, rivers, fields and roof clusters form distinct colour masses from above.

**World in Dreams use:** The regional overview: biomes and settlement density must stay legible before individual roofs matter.

**Boundary:** Use this degree of simplification for the distant map only; hexagonal tiles and railways are not proposed for this project.

Publisher-provided screenshot, retained here as a local research reference. Artwork belongs to its respective owners; it is not an original project asset.

items.title: 05 · A little enchantment
items.alt: A luminous forest uses warm focal light, cool vegetation and oversized organic shapes.
items.body:
**Early references · Trine 4: The Nightmare Prince**

**What to study:** A luminous forest uses warm focal light, cool vegetation and oversized organic shapes.

**World in Dreams use:** Elven, dryad and fairy habitats: architecture may follow trunks, roots and clearings.

**Boundary:** Lighting and habitat reference, not a settlement layout. Reduce glow and foreground clutter in overhead concepts.

Publisher-provided screenshot, retained here as a local research reference. Artwork belongs to its respective owners; it is not an original project asset.

items.title: 06 · A more fantastic city silhouette
items.alt: Bridges, towers and layered architecture emerge through coloured atmospheric depth.
items.body:
**Early references · Trine 4: The Nightmare Prince**

**What to study:** Bridges, towers and layered architecture emerge through coloured atmospheric depth.

**World in Dreams use:** A city-scale fantasy accent: one memorable skyline feature can distinguish a settlement.

**Boundary:** This is the most ornate edge of the selection. Keep ordinary districts simpler and use less fog so roads remain readable.

Publisher-provided screenshot, retained here as a local research reference. Artwork belongs to its respective owners; it is not an original project asset.

items.title: 07 · Architecture shaped by its inhabitants
items.alt: Water, terraces, cultivation and buildings visibly depend on each other.
items.body:
**Early references · Timberborn**

**What to study:** Water, terraces, cultivation and buildings visibly depend on each other.

**World in Dreams use:** A method for nonhuman settlements: adapt entrances, circulation, height and materials to the species and biome.

**Boundary:** Spatial reference only. Mechanical industry and beaver architecture are not part of the World in Dreams brief.

Publisher-provided screenshot, retained here as a local research reference. Artwork belongs to its respective owners; it is not an original project asset.
